response.text: In Option D, the UK family office settles PropCo Ltd into a discretionary trust, and PropCo Ltd owns the five commercial properties. The one-off costs at acquisition total £999,375: SDLT of £34,000 to £34,500 on each property, plus an inheritance-tax entry charge of £828,500 when the trust is set up. On exit, a buyer of the PropCo Ltd shares would pay stamp duty of £22,340, and the trust faces an inheritance-tax charge of up to £248,550 at every ten-year anniversary (that's the maximum rate, and reliefs and time-apportionment usually make it lower); no annual tax costs are shown in the figures. The £1,657,000 figure is only a comparator for what inheritance tax would be if the family held the assets personally, not a cost of this option. Please check with an adviser whether the settlor's residence and the post-April 2025 inheritance-tax rules bring the trust into scope, whether gifts in the last 7 years have already used the nil-rate band, and note that investment property does not qualify for business relief. The trust must also be registered on HMRC's Trust Registration Service, and a buyer inherits PropCo's history and the properties' original base cost.
